title: Hybrid and experimental experiences
summary: Experiences that combine player promises, loops, or mechanics from multiple families, or introduce a structure that does not fit a known family.

designKnowledge.principle: Compose from the player experience and dependencies between mechanics. Family labels help search and staffing; they are not templates or proof that two loops will work together.
compositionQuestions: Which resources and state transitions connect the loops?
Can one mechanic make another irrelevant or exploitable?
Which state is personal, party-owned, or world-owned?
What does a new player learn first?
coreLoop: introduce one loop at a time
revise the combination when one loop dominates
productionRisks: genre labels substitute for a complete design
the combination is cosmetic rather than changing decisions

technicalPatterns.name: Describe the composition as contracts
technicalPatterns.guidance: For each mechanic, record state ownership, inputs, outputs, dependencies, cancellation, authority, feedback, and acceptance evidence.

technicalPatterns.name: Preserve unknowns
technicalPatterns.guidance: When a combination has no verified reference, list the unknown and propose an isolated experiment instead of selecting the nearest package.

dependencies.rationale: Provides one family example for exploring composed player loops.
Provides an example with ownership, acquisition, and progression dependencies.
Provides an example with stateful decisions and multiplayer rule concerns.

failureModes.description: A hybrid is forced into a predefined package because one label looks familiar.
failureModes.mitigation: Write the player promise and state/resource contracts first; keep unmatched needs in the unknowns register.

failureModes.description: One loop invalidates another loop's choices or rewards.
failureModes.mitigation: Test each loop alone, then test cross-loop transitions and exploit cases with representative players.

scenarios.action: Ask a first-time player to explain the goal, current loop, and how a reward changes the next choice.
scenarios.expected: The player can explain the experience without relying on genre terminology.

scenarios.action: Exercise the principal cross-system transition, including cancellation, retry, and multiplayer contention.
scenarios.expected: Each system preserves its ownership rules and produces one understandable result.

acceptanceCriteria: Each linked mechanic has an owner and testable interface.
Unverified combinations remain unknown until evidence is produced.

considerations: Profile the integrated experience on midrange mobile and desktop.
Measure combined system cost; isolated mechanic budgets do not establish the integrated budget.

evidence.description: Composition questions, interface guidance, failure modes, and integration scenarios are defined.

assumptions: The taxonomy is extensible; a family label does not constrain implementation.
A new combination needs direct playtest and technical evidence before it becomes a verified pattern.
